case.case_title: Subbash Chandra Fernando v. Kapilaratne, Officer-in-Charge, Police Station, Gampaha and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1992] 1 Sri L.R. 305

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was arrested without being informed of the reason, violating Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was arrested without being informed of the reason, breaching Article 13(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The police had informed the petitioner of the charge against him, so there was no violation of Article 13(1).
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested on 19.07.89 on a complaint of assault under Emergency Regulations.
Petitioner alleged he was not informed of the reason for arrest when he went to the police station to complain.
Police notes and petitioner’s statement show he was informed of the charge.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 13(1) as requiring that a person arrested must be informed of the reason for arrest.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found from the police investigation notes and petitioner’s statement that the petitioner was informed of the charge, so no violation occurred.
principles_established: Arrest must be according to law and the arrested person must be informed of the reason.
Evidence such as police notes and statements are relevant to determine if the person was informed.

outcome.holding: No violation of Article 13(1) was found as the petitioner was informed of the reason for arrest.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) is central to the claim that the petitioner was arrested without being informed of the reason, which the court rejected based on evidence.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: It is clear from the notes of investigation and the petitioner’s statement to the police that the police had informed him of the charge against him; and as such there has been no violation of Article 13(1).
